children.text: Welcome to King Spa Virginia’s bathhouse and spa, where we invite you to celebrate and honor your body, mind, and soul through the healing powers of water and the ancient Korean tradition of communal bathing, socializing, and relaxing. Our gender-segregated bathhouses (separate from the rest of our spa) offer a way to deeply connect with your body and leave the worries of the world at the door. Here you’ll find a safe, welcoming atmosphere where every body is sacred, and everybody is welcome.

children.text: If you’ve never been to a communal bathhouse before, you might be in for a surprise when you see that nudity is required. And it takes a certain level of understanding of the traditions surrounding this practice, along with an open mind, to truly respect it and benefit from it. A Korean bathhouse, or jimjilbang, is a gender-segregated, communal bathing tradition that dates back over a thousand years and is still an important cultural practice in Korea today. It’s a wellness space where family and friends gather, indulging in self-care and relaxation while soaking in warm water, receiving a body scrub, or alternating between hot water, cold water, and steam.

heading.html: Why is Nudity Required in a Korean Bathhouse?

children.text: In Korea, communal bathing has deep cultural roots and is seen as a natural, normalized activity. Nudity in these spaces is not sexualized; instead, it’s viewed as part of a shared, respectful wellness experience. It fosters a sense of openness, equality, and comfort within the space. Here are some of the reasons why nudity is expected:

children.text: Wearing clothing—especially swimsuits—can carry bacteria, detergents, or oils that compromise the cleanliness of communal baths. Being nude helps maintain the water’s purity and ensures that everyone enters the pools as cleanly as possible after showering thoroughly.

In Korea, communal bathing has deep roots and is seen as a natural, normalized activity. Nudity in these spaces is not sexualized; instead, it’s viewed as part of a shared, respectful wellness experience. It fosters a sense of openness, equality, and comfort within the space.

Modern Korean bathhouses still follow long-standing customs where full immersion and skin-to-skin therapies (like body scrubs) are part of the ritual. Requiring nudity preserves the authenticity of the jjimjilbang experience.

heading.html: The Korean Bathhouse Experience at King Spa

children.text: King Spa’s Korean bathhouse in Virginia is thoughtfully designed to honor traditional practices while offering a clean, modern space for full-body renewal. Whether you’re seeking deep relaxation or a reset for your skin and muscles, our bathhouse areas provide the essentials for a classic jjimjilbang experience.

children.text: Move between warm and hot pools of various temperatures to relax muscles, reduce tension, and encourage circulation.
Refresh your body and stimulate your nervous system with a brisk dip—perfect between sauna or steam sessions.
Detoxify through deep, penetrating heat that opens pores and eases stress.
Begin and end your visit with a full cleanse—an essential step before entering shared waters.
Professionally performed exfoliation treatments that remove dead skin cells and leave you feeling refreshed and polished.

heading.html: Bath House Benefits for Body, Mind, & Soul

children.text: Visiting a bath house is more than just a relaxing escape—it’s a holistic wellness practice with physical and mental health benefits. There’s a reason why they call it hydro-therapy, because spending time in and around water has a deeply therapeutic effect on us. You can experience these benefits first-hand when you visit our Korean bathhouse in VA:

children.cls: elementor-section elementor-inner-section elementor-element elementor-element-116e1f7e womens-body-scrub active elementor-section-boxed elementor-section-height-default elementor-section-height-default

children.html:
Improved Circulation

Alternating between hot tubs and cold plunge pools encourages healthy blood flow and cardiovascular function.

Muscle Recovery

Warm water and steam help relax tight muscles and joints, making it ideal for post-workout recovery or general soreness.

Skin Detox and Renewal

Steam rooms and exfoliating body scrubs remove dead skin cells and clear pores, leaving your skin soft, smooth, and refreshed.

Stress Relief

Immersing yourself in water and quiet space helps reduce cortisol levels and mental fatigue.

Respiratory Support

Steam therapy can ease breathing, especially for guests experiencing mild congestion or sinus pressure.

Natural Energy Boost

The hot-cold contrast stimulates your nervous system and can leave you feeling recharged and more alert.

children.html:
Do I need to be nude in the bathhouse?

Yes. In keeping with traditional Korean bathhouse customs and for hygiene reasons, nudity is required in the gender-specific bathhouse areas. Spa uniforms are provided for use outside of these zones.

Are the bathhouse areas co-ed?

No. Our bathhouse is gender-segregated and can be found in both the men and women’s locker rooms. The rest of our spa is co-ed which includes our saunas, lounge areas, outdoor bade pool, and indoor Aqua pool. Swimwear is required in our outdoor bade pool and Aqua pool.

Do I need a reservation for the bathhouse?

No reservations are needed for general bathhouse access. Entry is included in admission. Body scrub services and V-Steams are also first-come, first-served and must be booked onsite (additional fees for these services are required).

What is a body scrub and is it included?

Body scrubs are full-body exfoliation treatments performed by trained professionals. They are not included with admission and are available as an optional add-on. You can book your body scrub treatment inside the women’s locker room.

What are V-Steams and where are they offered?

V-Steams are steam-based wellness treatments offered in the women’s bathhouse only. They involve sitting over a warm, herbal steam to support circulation and feminine care. You can book your V-Steam session inside the women’s locker room.

Are there showers inside the bathhouse?

Yes, there are showers inside the bathhouse area and we ask all guests to shower off before using any of our facilities, hot tubs, or pools.

Do I have to go to the bathhouse when I visit King Spa?

No – visiting our bathhouse is completely optional. You can skip this area and head straight to our saunas and pools if you’d like. The choice is yours.
